evidence.quote: Both alloys were prepared by melting in an electric furnace under a protective salt flux using high purity elemental Mg and Zn and Mg-Y and Mg-Gd master alloys.
Ingots were cast into a steel mold of diameter 42 mm, suitable for extrusion.
As-cast WZ72Gd1 samples were extruded at 623 K (350 °C) at a ram speed of 30 mm/min and reduction ratio of 18:1 (designated R18, total strain eT = 2.9).
Other cast samples were given the same homogenization treatment, followed by slow cooling, before extrusion at 623 K (350 °C) with an extrusion ratio of 4:1 (designated TT+R4, total strain eT = 1.4).

evidence.quote: Following the homogenizing annealing at 808 K (535 °C) and slow cool, Figure 1(b), fine plate precipitates appear (bright) within the Mg dendrites and the measured fraction of blocky LPSO phase decorating the interdendritic regions was reduced to 12 ± 2 pct.

evidence.quote: For both alloys, the measured volume fraction of fine recrystallized grains after R4 extrusion was similar, 34 ± 2 pct, indicating that this depends on the total processing strain rather than the prior microstructure (fine precipitates or not). After such processing, the average recrystallized grain sizes measured were about 0.76 lm in the Gd-containing alloy, compared to 1.2 lm for the previously studied WZ72 alloy.
After eight ECAP passes, the comminution of the LPSO plates results in a distribution of very fine particles with a size about 150 to 200 nm, Figure 3(c).
